title: Acacia as the Tree of Life in Egypt, Freemasonry and the Ark of the Covenant

tellings.quote: life or the the acacia tree being the Tree of Life in Egypt and then in Freemasonry The Acacia Leaf is is a big is a kind of place prominent it plays a role in Freemasonry and um there's there's no doubt about it the wood out of which the Ark of the Covenant was made was acacia wood

plain: The acacia tree, the story goes, was the Tree of Life in ancient Egypt, its leaf holds a prominent place in the symbols of Freemasonry (a centuries-old fraternal society with secret rituals), and the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Hebrew Bible said to hold the tablets of the law, was made of acacia wood. Michels draws these links himself in a conversation with the writer Graham Hancock, whom he credits. The suggestion is that one sacred symbol may run through Egyptian, biblical and Masonic tradition.
